numerical_failure.observed_behavior: UECMResults.resid inherited the parent class residual computation and returned endog minus fittedvalues, i.e. residuals computed against the levels series (model.endog) instead of the differenced series, producing values close to the level values of the series.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: UECMResults.resid should compute model._y - fittedvalues, i.e. residuals against the differenced dependent variable (first difference of endog) in the UECM equation.
trigger_conditions: Accessing resid on a UECMResults object (UECM model fit)
The dependent variable in the UECM equation is the first difference of endog stored in model._y, while the inherited resid used model.endog
Test case uses dane_data with UECM lags {lry: 1, ibo: 3, ide: 2}
oracle_clues: Issue #9793 notes residuals close to the level values of the series, making Durbin-Watson and Breusch-Godfrey diagnostics incorrect
PR #9812 adds test test_uecm_resid asserting np.testing.assert_allclose(res.resid, res.model._y - res.fittedvalues) with default tolerance; no explicit tolerance given
The fix overrides resid as a property in UECMResults (diff changes @cache_readonly to @property in statsmodels/tsa/ardl/model.py around lines 2100-2106)
No concrete numerical input/output values are given in the passages

category_specific_evidence: UECMResults.resid returned residuals computed against levels (model.endog) instead of the differenced dependent variable model._y, per issue #9793.
The stated correct formula is residual = model._y - fittedvalues (differenced series minus fitted values), replacing the inherited endog - fittedvalues.
Diagnostics such as Durbin-Watson and Breusch-Godfrey were described as incorrect because the residuals were close to the level values of the series.
The diff changes the resid decorator from @cache_readonly to @property in statsmodels/tsa/ardl/model.py.
The added test test_uecm_resid asserts np.testing.assert_allclose(res.resid, res.model._y - res.fittedvalues) using dane_data with UECM lags {lry: 1, ibo: 3, ide: 2}.
No concrete numerical values (expected residuals, magnitudes) or tolerance are given in the passages beyond the default assert_allclose comparison.
reproduction_risks: The PR body notes the test was originally missing and that the test was added later in commits; the passages do not confirm the pre-fix test failure on main.
The issue update says the fix was implemented but not backported to the stable release, so the version exhibiting the bug is not stated.
Exact tolerance for assert_allclose is not specified (default rtol/atol used), and dane_data contents are not provided in the passages.
